competences: The learner identifies and describes the main features of the national flag from the source material.
The learner explains how the national flag relates to Uganda's national identity.
languageCompetence: Learners pronounce, spell, read and write: National flag, emblem, crested crane, brotherhood, flagpole, half-mast, mourning.
objectives: By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to identify the main facts about the national flag.
By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to answer at least four sourced questions correctly about the national flag.
priorKnowledge: Learners know that Uganda attained independence and can name at least one symbol of the country.
materials: Chart showing the Uganda national flag
Black, yellow, red and white paper strips
references: P.5 Social Studies Lesson Notes Term III: Uganda as an Independent Nation

steps.teacherActivity: The teacher recalls the previous work and asks: "What is the name of the bird in the middle of the Uganda flag?" Learners' first responses introduce the national flag in the topic Uganda as an independent nation. The teacher establishes what learners already understand.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners recall earlier work about Uganda, answer the opening question and connect their responses with today's new sub-topic.

steps.stage: Development: Symbols of an independent nation
steps.content: National symbols are features that identify a particular country. Uganda's national symbols include the national flag. Other symbols include the national anthem and coat of arms. The national motto and constitution are also national symbols.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher uses the chart showing the uganda national flag to teach symbols of an independent nation. They put the exact sourced points on the board: "National symbols are features that identify a particular country. Uganda's national symbols include the national flag." They check understanding with the question: "Give one way the National flag is respected." and explain the relevant terms.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners observe the material, identify the listed facts, respond to the teacher's question and copy the organised notes into their exercise books.

steps.content: The national flag identifies Uganda as an independent nation. Its main colours are black, yellow and red. Black represents the black African people of Uganda. Yellow represents Uganda's abundant sunshine. Red represents international brotherhood among people. The white circle represents peace. The circle contains Uganda's crested crane emblem. Grace Ibingira designed Uganda's national flag. The national flag first replaced the Union Jack in 1962.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher uses the chart showing the uganda national flag to teach the uganda national flag. They put the exact sourced points on the board: "The national flag identifies Uganda as an independent nation. Its main colours are black, yellow and red." They check understanding with the question: "How does the red colour of the Uganda promote unity world wide?" and explain the relevant terms.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners observe the material, identify the listed facts, respond to the teacher's question and copy the organised notes into their exercise books.

steps.stage: Development: Places and occasions for displaying the flag
steps.content: The national flag is flown at schools. It is flown at government offices. It is flown at airports and police stations. It is flown at embassies and high commissions. The flag identifies Uganda at important public events. Half-mast flying may mark national mourning.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher uses the chart showing the uganda national flag to teach places and occasions for displaying the flag. They put the exact sourced points on the board: "The national flag is flown at schools. It is flown at government offices." They check understanding with the question: "Identify the last colour of the Uganda National flag." and explain the relevant terms.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners observe the material, identify the listed facts, respond to the teacher's question and copy the organised notes into their exercise books.

steps.stage: Development: Ways of respecting the national flag
steps.content: People stand still while the flag is raised or lowered. The flag must not touch the ground. The flag should not be used as clothing. The flag should not be used for commercial advertising. The crested crane faces the flagpole when the flag is raised.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher uses the chart showing the uganda national flag to teach ways of respecting the national flag. They put the exact sourced points on the board: "People stand still while the flag is raised or lowered. The flag must not touch the ground." They check understanding with the question: "Give two importance of A national flag." and explain the relevant terms.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners observe the material, identify the listed facts, respond to the teacher's question and copy the organised notes into their exercise books.

steps.content: Sourced exercise: What is the name of the bird in the middle of the Uganda flag? | Give one way the National flag is respected. | How does the red colour of the Uganda promote unity world wide? | Identify the last colour of the Uganda National flag.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher writes the exercise questions on the board, beginning with "What is the name of the bird in the middle of the Uganda flag?" and "Give one way the National flag is respected.". They observe individual work, assist pupils with difficulty and check answers against the lesson content.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners answer sourced written questions individually, look back at the copied points and correct inaccurate answers during the marking exercise.

steps.teacherActivity: The teacher asks: "How does the red colour of the Uganda promote unity world wide?" and "Identify the last colour of the Uganda National flag." They confirm the source-based answers, correct misunderstandings, and connect these facts to Uganda's independent national identity.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners give short oral answers, explain an important fact about the lesson and correct errors they made in their written work.

assessment: Mark the written and oral sourced questions: "What is the name of the bird in the middle of the Uganda flag?" "Give one way the National flag is respected." and "How does the red colour of the Uganda promote unity world wide?" Compare the learners' answers with the lesson points and passages.
homework: Finish the sourced exercise in the learner's book, including this question: "Why does the crested crane on the Uganda flag stand on one leg?"
